title: Orchestrator upgrade sequencing timeout caused cross-cluster connectivity cascade
creator: Sana Rodriguez
description: Summary: During a staged rollout of private orchestrator 2.7.0 to 18 customer VPC clusters, an upgrade sequencing timeout triggered cascading control-plane disconnects for a subset of clusters. The incident caused 7 clusters to briefly lose API connectivity (3–12 minutes), degraded autoscaling for dedicated pools, and increased request error rates against hosted fallbacks. This ticket captures the timeline, root cause analysis, and concrete follow-ups to prevent recurrence.
timeline:
2026-03-09 22:05 UTC: Canary wave 1 rollout starts.
2026-03-09 22:47 UTC: First orchestrator pod in cluster-7 repeatedly failing readiness checks; on-call notices increased reconcile latencies.
2026-03-09 23:02 UTC: Control-plane pod restarts spread to cluster-7 and cluster-12 after rollout controller retried a migration job.
2026-03-09 23:15 UTC: DNS resolutions in affected clusters began sporadic failures (kube-dns TTL mismatch observed).
2026-03-09 23:28 UTC: Autoscaler for dedicated pools reported capacity oscillation (5xx spike) and shed traffic to hosted fallback policies.
2026-03-09 23:40 UTC: Rollout paused globally. Engineering rollback to orch-2.6.4 initiated.
2026-03-09 23:50 UTC: Connectivity gradually restored; final cluster healthy at 2026-03-10 00:02 UTC.
root_cause: The orchestrator upgrade introduced a new deterministic migration step that performs an ordered CRD write + leader transfer between controller replicas. The migration step used a 20s per-node sequencing timeout that was insufficient for clusters with high kube-apiserver load and conservative DNS TTL settings. When the leader transfer timed out, controllers retried aggressively and concurrently across nodes. That retry storm increased API server load, exacerbated DNS cache divergence (pods observed stale SRV/Endpoints because upstream kube-dns caches were TTL-limited), and caused pod readiness gates to fail. In short: brittle sequencing + low timeout + implicit retry concurrency + DNS TTL misalignment produced a cascading availability failure.
impact: 7 private VPC clusters experienced control-plane API 502/504 responses for between 3 and 12 minutes. Customer-facing symptoms: transient 5xx errors for inference requests routed via dedicated pools, delayed scaling decisions (slow upscales), and increased tail latency for RPCs to orchestrator. No data loss observed. Several enterprise customers opened high-severity support tickets during the window.
resolution: Immediate actions taken during incident: global rollout paused at 23:40 UTC, operators manually forced migration to sequential mode for canaries and applied a temporary 120s sequencing grace window for affected clusters. We rolled back orchestrator to 2.6.4 for impacted customers where automated mitigation did not stabilize within 10 minutes. Post-incident patch released (orch-2.7.1) that disables aggressive concurrent retries and exposes sequencing timeout as a configuration knob.
followup_notes: During post-incident review we validated that clusters with conservative DNS TTLs (< 30s) and large control-plane watch counts were more likely to hit the timeout. The incident exposes three orthogonal risks: (1) hard-coded sequencing timeouts in the orchestrator, (2) implicit global concurrency amplification from retries, and (3) brittle coupling between control-plane upgrades and customer kube-dns configurations. We need both product changes and ops guardrails.
action_items: (A1) Make sequencing timeout configurable per-cluster and increase default to 90s. Owner: @Ethan M. Target: 2026-03-18.
(A2) Add exponential backoff with jitter to migration retries to avoid synchronized retry storms. Owner: @Maya Singh. PR: github.com/redwood-inference/orchestrator/pull/12987. Target: 2026-03-17.
(A3) Implement a rollout throttler that limits concurrent migration jobs across nodes in the same cluster. Owner: @Julian Park. Estimate: 5 points. Target: 2026-03-24.
(A4) Run a diagnostic job preflight that checks kube-apiserver QPS, watch counts, and kube-dns TTLs before enabling non-backward-compatible migrations. Owner: @Priya Kapoor. Target: 2026-03-20.
(A5) Update private deployment runbook and on-call playbook: add explicit steps for pausing rollouts, increasing sequencing grace, and manual rollback. Owner: @SRE. Due: 2026-03-15.

(A6) Customer communication: send targeted post-incident summaries and mitigations to affected accounts; include recommended kube-dns TTL guidance for private clusters. Owner: @Customer Success. Due: 2026-03-14.
(A7) Add observability: create Grafana panel for 'migration sequencing latency' and alert when sequential migrations exceed 60s in a cluster. Owner: @Instrumentation. Target: 2026-03-19.
(A8) Run a blue/green canary that intentionally flips leader roles under load to validate sequencing behavior prior to next rollout. Owner: @Ethan M. Target: 2026-04-01.
(A9) Add an integration test that simulates kube-dns cache divergence and verifies orchestrator migration backoff behaves as designed. Owner: @QA. Target: 2026-03-28.
review_feedback: PM and SRE suggested adding customer-safe default settings and an opt-out flag for aggressive migrations. Design requested clearer UX in the Console for 'Upgrade health' per cluster. Security noted no secrets exposure but asked that the preflight checks include KMS connectivity verification. Engineers recommended a follow-up spike to test sequencing under scaled-up API server load.
postmortem_status: Draft - awaiting SRE validation and PM approval before publishing to Confluence.
notes_for_release: orch-2.7.1: disable concurrent retry default, expose sequencing timeout, add metrics for migration latency. Communicate to Dedicated/Private customers the upgrade window and preflight checklist.
customer_impact_summary: High-priority incident affecting 7 private clusters; short-duration outage for control-plane operations resulting in increased inference error rates for affected customers. No persisted data loss; mitigations and rollback restored service within 12 minutes for the last impacted cluster.
post_incident_retrospective: Key learning: stateful sequenced changes that depend on leader transfer must assume variable control-plane latency across customer environments. Future rollouts will default to conservative sequencing with opt-in aggressive modes for low-risk clusters. We'll also add more preflight cluster health gating to prevent automatic upgrades when kube-dns or API-server load heuristics are out of recommended range.
